perf-bot: [nightly] perf alert for route=gen-short-tokens: 95p latency +2.4x vs baseline (window start 2024-11-03T02:30Z). KV cache hit rate dropped 87% -> 44% on the same window. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/perf/alerts/1801234567 :rotating_light: tagging #eng-runtime

morgan: saw this. thanks for the ping. any idea which merges landed in the last 24h that touch prefetch/batching/kernel-selector?

kai: yep — PR merged ~01:40Z: "rpc-kv-prefetch" (commit abc1234). It tightened prefetch heuristics and explicitly disables prefetch for seq_len <= 64 to avoid spurious warms. Could interact with kernel selector heuristics.

devon: starting a local repro now with small seqs. command I'm using:
```bash
./perf/run_repro.sh --model alpha --seq 32 --concurrency 16 --iters 2000
```
Will post logs in a sec.

devon: log snippet (KV stats + kernel picks):
```
[2024-11-03T02:38:11Z] KV_CACHE: hit_rate=0.46, misses=540, hits=460
[2024-11-03T02:38:11Z] KERNEL_SELECTOR: chosen=grouped_fft, reason="batch_score=1.8 > alt=1.2"
[2024-11-03T02:38:11Z] LATENCY: p95=120ms, p50=20ms
```

sarah: hmm grouped_fft for seq=32 is surprising. kernel selector change from earlier patch prefers larger kernels at small batch sizes, I think. grouped_fft is efficient when cache warm, but degrades on cold KV misses (extra overhead). if prefetch disabled -> more KV misses -> grouped_fft loses.

morgan: can we canary a rollback of rpc-kv-prefetch in dedicated? prefer to avoid full revert if we can patch selector quickly, but need to stop customer impact.

kai: kicked off the CI perf job comparing main vs main~1 (before merge). CI perf job: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/1801234567. Bisect points at commit d4f9b7e which adjusted batching_heuristics.py:score_for_kernel to bias towards larger kernels.

devon: numbers from my repro with prefetch disabled vs prefetch restored:
- prefetch disabled: p50 20ms, p95 120ms
- prefetch enabled: p50 18ms, p95 94ms
So p95 regressed ~28ms (≈30%). KV hit diff matches perf-bot numbers.

ops-bot: Automated note: canary rollback window available. To proceed run `/ops rollback canary rpc-kv-prefetch` (requires two approvals).

sarah: proposed hotfix: re-enable prefetch for seq <= 64 (restore previous prefetch window) and add a guard in kernel selector: if recent_kv_miss_rate > 0.3 prefer fallback_kernel. Also add a perf regression unit test that simulates KV miss burst.

kai: I'll open PR (WIP) with revert+guard, link: https://git.internal/redwood/pr/4782. tagging @morgan for canary go-ahead.

morgan: approved. let's do canary rollback first (safest). After canary confirms, we can merge a more targeted change. Please include changelog note about kernel-selector interplay.

devon: canary rollback applied at 2024-11-03T03:12Z. running quick perf check now.

devon: canary results: p95 back to 96ms, hit_rate=85%. baseline restored. https://dash.internal/redwood/perf/runs/1801234567-canary

perf-bot: [resolved] alert for thread 1801234567: latency and KV metrics returned to baseline after canary rollback. Closing. :white_check_mark:
